title: Entropy & Spontaneity (Second Law of Thermodynamics, Entropy, Gibbs Energy, & Equilibrium Criteria)
syllabus: Spontaneous and non-spontaneous processes; Limitations of the First Law of Thermodynamics; Second Law of Thermodynamics; Concept of entropy (S) as a measure of disorder/randomness; State function nature of entropy; Calculation of entropy change (ΔS = q_rev / T); Entropy changes in phase transitions (fusion, vaporization, sublimation) and Trouton's rule; Entropy changes during expansion/compression of ideal gases; Total entropy change of system and surroundings (ΔS_total = ΔS_sys + ΔS_surr) as criterion for spontaneity; Gibbs free energy (G = H - TS); Gibbs energy change (ΔG = ΔH - TΔS) and Gibbs-Helmholtz equation; Criteria for spontaneity and equilibrium under conditions of constant T and P (ΔG < 0 for spontaneity, ΔG = 0 for equilibrium, ΔG > 0 for non-spontaneous); Effect of temperature on reaction spontaneity (signs of ΔH and ΔS); Standard Gibbs free energy change (ΔrG°) and its relation to the equilibrium constant K (ΔrG° = -2.303 RT log K); Third Law of Thermodynamics and absolute entropies (residual entropy concept)

questions.question: [NEET 2023] For a chemical reaction, the change in enthalpy is $\Delta H = -10.0\text{ kJ/mol}$ and the change in entropy is $\Delta S = -20.0\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$. At what temperature will the reaction attain equilibrium ($\Delta G = 0$)?
questions.solution:
At dynamic equilibrium, the Gibbs free energy change is zero:
$$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = 0 \implies T = \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$$
Convert $\Delta H$ to Joules:
$$\Delta H = -10.0\text{ kJ/mol} = -10000\text{ J/mol}$$
$$\Delta S = -20.0\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$
Calculate equilibrium temperature $T$:
$$T = \frac{-10000\text{ J/mol}}{-20.0\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}} = 500\text{ K}$$
(Above $500\text{ K}$, the reaction becomes non-spontaneous; below $500\text{ K}$, it is spontaneous).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] For an isolated system undergoing a spontaneous process, which of the following statements is strictly TRUE?
questions.solution:
1. For an **isolated system**, there is neither exchange of heat nor work with the surroundings ($q = 0, w = 0$). By the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$$\Delta U = q + w = 0 + 0 = 0$$
2. According to the **Second Law of Thermodynamics**, all spontaneous (natural) processes occurring in an isolated system are accompanied by an increase in total entropy (disorder):
$$\Delta S_{\text{isolated}} > 0$$
Therefore, $\Delta U = 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] The standard Gibbs free energy change for a reversible reaction at $300\text{ K}$ is $\Delta_r G^\circ = -11.5\text{ kJ/mol}$. The value of the equilibrium constant $K$ for this reaction is: (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}, 2.303 \times R \times 300 \approx 5744\text{ J/mol}, 10^2 = 100$)
questions.solution:
The relation between $\Delta_r G^\circ$ and equilibrium constant $K$ is:
$$\Delta_r G^\circ = -2.303\, RT \log_{10} K$$
Given:
- $\Delta_r G^\circ = -11.5\text{ kJ/mol} = -11500\text{ J/mol}$
- $2.303 RT = 2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \approx 5744\text{ J/mol}$
$$\log_{10} K = \frac{-\Delta_r G^\circ}{2.303\, RT} = \frac{-(-11500)}{5744} \approx 2.0$$
$$K = 10^{2.0} = 1.0 \times 10^2 = 100$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] In which of the following transformations does the entropy of the system DECREASE ($\Delta S < 0$)?
options: Crystallization of liquid water into solid ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$
Sublimation of solid iodine into violet vapors
Dissolution of crystalline sugar in water
questions.solution:
Entropy measures the randomness or degree of microstate disorder in a system:
1. Freezing of water: Liquid water molecules have higher translational/rotational freedom. In ice, they are locked into an orderly, rigid open crystalline lattice, so entropy decreases ($\Delta S < 0$).
2. Sublimation of $\text{I}_2(s) \rightarrow \text{I}_2(g)$ produces highly disordered gas ($\Delta S > 0$).
3. Dissolution of sugar breaks crystalline order into dispersed solute particles ($\Delta S > 0$).
4. $\text{CaCO}_3(s) \rightarrow \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$ generates $1\text{ mole}$ of gas from pure solid ($\Delta n_g = +1$), so entropy increases ($\Delta S > 0$).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] For a reaction to be spontaneous at ALL temperatures, the signs of enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and entropy change ($\Delta S$) must be:
questions.solution:
The criterion for spontaneity at constant temperature and pressure is $\Delta G < 0$:
$$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$$
1. If $\Delta H < 0$ (exothermic) and $\Delta S > 0$ (entropy increasing):
- $\Delta H$ is negative.
- The term $-T\Delta S$ is strictly negative (since absolute temperature $T > 0\text{ K}$).
2. Therefore, $\Delta G = (\text{negative}) + (\text{negative}) < 0$ at all temperatures.
The process is unconditionally spontaneous at all temperatures.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The boiling point of liquid ethanol is $78.3^\circ\text{C}$ ($351.45\text{ K}$), and its standard molar enthalpy of vaporization is $\Delta_{\text{vap}}H = 38.6\text{ kJ/mol}$. The standard molar entropy of vaporization ($\Delta_{\text{vap}}S$) of ethanol is:
questions.solution:
At the normal boiling point, liquid and vapor are in thermodynamic equilibrium ($\Delta G = 0$):
$$\Delta_{\text{vap}}S = \frac{\Delta_{\text{vap}}H}{T_b}$$
Substitute $\Delta_{\text{vap}}H = 38.6\text{ kJ/mol} = 38600\text{ J/mol}$ and $T_b = 351.45\text{ K}$:
$$\Delta_{\text{vap}}S = \frac{38600\text{ J/mol}}{351.45\text{ K}} \approx +109.83\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Which of the following conditions represents the fundamental criterion for dynamic equilibrium in a system maintained at constant temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
Criteria for thermodynamic states at constant $T$ and $P$:
1. **Spontaneous process:** $(\Delta G)_{T, P} < 0$ (Gibbs free energy decreases to a minimum).
2. **Equilibrium state:** $(\Delta G)_{T, P} = 0$ (Gibbs free energy reaches its minimum value; $dG = 0$).
3. **Non-spontaneous process:** $(\Delta G)_{T, P} > 0$.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A reaction is endothermic ($\Delta H > 0$) and proceeds with an increase in entropy ($\Delta S > 0$). This reaction will be spontaneous at:
questions.solution:
From the Gibbs equation:
$$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$$
Given $\Delta H > 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$:
- For spontaneity, we require $\Delta G < 0$:
$$\Delta H - T\Delta S < 0 \implies T\Delta S > \Delta H \implies T > \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$$
At high temperatures, the positive entropy factor ($T\Delta S$) dominates over the positive enthalpy term ($\Delta H$), making $\Delta G$ negative.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] The Third Law of Thermodynamics states that:
options: The entropy of any pure, perfectly crystalline substance approaches zero as absolute zero temperature ($0\text{ K}$) is approached
The energy of the universe is constant while its entropy tends toward a maximum
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
Absolute zero temperature can be attained by infinite isothermal cycles
questions.solution:
The **Third Law of Thermodynamics** (formulated by Walther Nernst and Max Planck) states that:
'The entropy of a perfectly crystalline, chemically pure substance is exactly zero at the absolute zero of temperature ($T = 0\text{ K}$)'
$$\lim_{T \to 0} S = 0$$
This provides an absolute reference point to determine standard absolute molar entropies ($S^\circ$) of substances.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] For the reaction $2\text{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$, $\Delta H = -57.2\text{ kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta S = -175.8\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$. At $298\text{ K}$, the value of $\Delta G$ is:
questions.solution:
Using the Gibbs equation:
$$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$$
Given:
- $\Delta H = -57.2\text{ kJ/mol} = -57200\text{ J/mol}$
- $T = 298\text{ K}$
- $\Delta S = -175.8\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$
Calculate $T\Delta S$:
$$T\Delta S = 298 \times (-175.8) = -52388.4\text{ J/mol} = -52.39\text{ kJ/mol}$$
$$\Delta G = -57.2 - (-52.39) = -57.2 + 52.39 = -4.81\text{ kJ/mol}$$
Because $\Delta G < 0$, dimerization of $\text{NO}_2$ to $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ is spontaneous at $298\text{ K}$.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] When an ideal gas undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion from volume $V_1$ to $V_2$, the change in entropy of the gas is given by:
questions.solution:
1. For an isothermal reversible process involving an ideal gas: $\Delta U = 0$.
2. From the First Law: $q_{\text{rev}} = -w_{\text{rev}} = nRT \ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$.
3. Entropy change is defined as:
$$\Delta S = \frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T} = \frac{nRT \ln(V_2/V_1)}{T} = nR \ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$$
(In terms of common logarithm: $\Delta S = 2.303\, nR \log_{10}(V_2/V_1)$).

questions.question: Which of the following substances has a NON-ZERO residual entropy at absolute zero ($0\text{ K}$) due to crystalline orientation disorder?
questions.solution:
1. The Third Law holds strictly for perfectly ordered crystals without geometric degeneracy.
2. In solid carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$), because the dipole moment is very small and the sizes of $\text{C}$ and $\text{O}$ are comparable, molecules freeze with random end-to-end orientations ($\text{C}-\text{O}\cdots\text{C}-\text{O}$ or $\text{C}-\text{O}\cdots\text{O}-\text{C}$).
3. Each molecule has two equally probable orientations ($W = 2^N$), resulting in a non-zero **residual entropy** at $0\text{ K}$:
$$S_0 = k_B \ln W = k_B \ln(2^{N_A}) = R \ln 2 \approx 5.76\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$
(Other examples include $\text{NO}, \text{N}_2\text{O},$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ice).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] If a process has $\Delta H > 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$, the process is:
options: Spontaneous only at very high temperatures
Spontaneous only at very low temperatures
questions.solution:
From $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$:
- $\Delta H > 0$ (positive)
- Since $\Delta S < 0$, the term $-T\Delta S$ is positive for all $T > 0\text{ K}$.
$$\Delta G = (\text{positive}) + (\text{positive}) > 0 \quad (\text{always positive})$$
Because $\Delta G$ can never be negative at any physical temperature, the process is **non-spontaneous at all temperatures**.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] For the reaction $\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)$, the signs of $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
1. Decomposition of $\text{PCl}_5$ into $\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ involves the cleavage of two axial $\text{P}-\text{Cl}$ bonds, requiring an input of thermal energy $\implies$ endothermic, $\Delta H > 0$.
2. The reaction produces $2\text{ moles}$ of gaseous products from $1\text{ mole}$ of gaseous reactant ($\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 1 = +1$), increasing the degree of molecular disorder $\implies \Delta S > 0$.
Therefore, both $\Delta H > 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] What is the total entropy change ($\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{sys}} + \Delta S_{\text{surr}}$) for any reversible thermodynamic process occurring in the universe?
questions.solution:
1. For a reversible process, heat lost by surroundings equals heat gained by system ($q_{\text{surr}} = -q_{\text{sys}}$) at the same temperature $T$.
2. $\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = \frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$ and $\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = -\frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$.
3. Therefore, for any **reversible process**:
$$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{sys}} + \Delta S_{\text{surr}} = 0$$
(For an irreversible spontaneous process, the Clausius inequality requires $\Delta S_{\text{total}} > 0$).

questions.question: [NEET 2021] The enthalpy of fusion of water is $6.0\text{ kJ/mol}$ at $0^\circ\text{C}$ ($273.15\text{ K}$). The entropy change for the melting of $1\text{ mole}$ of ice is:
questions.solution:
At the normal melting point ($T_f = 273.15\text{ K}$), solid ice and liquid water are in equilibrium:
$$\Delta_{\text{fus}}S = \frac{\Delta_{\text{fus}}H}{T_f}$$
$$\Delta_{\text{fus}}S = \frac{6000\text{ J/mol}}{273.15\text{ K}} \approx +21.966\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1} \approx +21.96\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An equilibrium constant $K$ for a reaction is $1.0$ at $298\text{ K}$. The standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta_r G^\circ$) for this reaction is:
questions.solution:
The relation between $\Delta_r G^\circ$ and equilibrium constant $K$ is:
$$\Delta_r G^\circ = -2.303\, RT \log_{10} K$$
When $K = 1.0$:
$$\log_{10}(1.0) = 0$$
$$\Delta_r G^\circ = -2.303\, RT \times 0 = 0$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When egg white is boiled and hardens (denaturation of albumin protein), what happens to the entropy of the protein?
options: Entropy increases, because the compact native globular helical structure unfolds into a random, disorganized coil
Entropy decreases, because the liquid albumin solidifies into a solid gel
Entropy initially decreases and then reaches zero
questions.solution:
1. In native globular albumin, polypeptide chains are tightly folded into highly ordered, compact, helical and pleated secondary/tertiary structures with specific hydrogen bonds.
2. On boiling, thermal energy disrupts the stabilizing hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions.
3. The polypeptide chains unfold and uncoil into disordered, random three-dimensional conformations (denaturation).
4. This large gain in conformational randomness results in an **increase in entropy** ($\Delta S > 0$), despite the apparent physical hardening/coagulation of the egg white.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] For an irreversible spontaneous process at constant $T$ and $P$, which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
1. The Clausius statement of the Second Law dictates that the total entropy of the universe increases in any spontaneous natural process: $\Delta S_{\text{total}} > 0$.
2. Under conditions of constant temperature and pressure, the total entropy change relates to Gibbs free energy by:
$$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = -\frac{\Delta G_{\text{sys}}}{T}$$
3. Since $T$ is in Kelvin ($T > 0$), $\Delta S_{\text{total}} > 0$ requires:
$$\Delta G_{\text{sys}} < 0$$
Both represent equivalent criteria for spontaneity.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A reaction has $\Delta H = -40.0\text{ kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta S = -80.0\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Above what temperature will the reaction become NON-SPONTANEOUS?
questions.solution:
For spontaneity:
$$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$$
$$-40000 - T(-80.0) < 0$$
$$-40000 + 80.0\, T < 0$$
$$80.0\, T < 40000 \implies T < 500\text{ K}$$
- The reaction is spontaneous below $500\text{ K}$.
- At $T = 500\text{ K}$, it reaches equilibrium ($\Delta G = 0$).
- Above $500\text{ K}$, $\Delta G > 0$, and the reaction becomes **non-spontaneous**.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following thermodynamic properties is a PATH FUNCTION?
options: Heat exchanged in an irreversible process ($q$)
questions.solution:
1. A **path function** depends on the specific mechanism or route taken between two thermodynamic states.
2. Heat ($q$) and work ($w$) are classic path functions.
3. Entropy ($S$), Gibbs free energy ($G$), and enthalpy ($H$) depend exclusively on the state variables of the system and are **state functions**.

questions.question:
[NEET 2020] The standard entropy of $X_2, Y_2,$ and $XY_3$ are $60, 40,$ and $50\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. For the reaction:
$$\frac{1}{2}X_2 + \frac{3}{2}Y_2 \rightarrow XY_3; \quad \Delta H = -30\text{ kJ}$$
To be in equilibrium, the temperature should be:
questions.solution:
1. Calculate $\Delta_r S^\circ$:
$$\Delta_r S^\circ = S^\circ(XY_3) - \left[\frac{1}{2}S^\circ(X_2) + \frac{3}{2}S^\circ(Y_2)\right]$$
$$\Delta_r S^\circ = 50 - \left[\frac{1}{2}(60) + \frac{3}{2}(40)\right] = 50 - [30 + 60] = 50 - 90 = -40\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$
2. At equilibrium, $\Delta G = 0 \implies T = \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$:
$$T = \frac{-30000\text{ J}}{-40\text{ J/K}} = 750\text{ K}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] What is the entropy change of the surroundings when $1\text{ mole}$ of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly at $300\text{ K}$ from $10\text{ L}$ to $100\text{ L}$?
questions.solution:
1. For isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas:
$$\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = 2.303\, nR \log_{10}\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right) = 2.303 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times \log_{10}\left(\frac{100}{10}\right) = 19.14\text{ J/K}$$
2. In a reversible process, $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{sys}} + \Delta S_{\text{surr}} = 0$:
$$\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = -\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = -19.14\text{ J/K}$$

questions.question:
[NEET 2021] For the conversion of water to steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ pressure:
$$\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$$
The values of $\Delta G, \Delta H,$ and $\Delta S$ are:
questions.solution:
At the normal boiling point ($100^\circ\text{C}, 1\text{ atm}$):
1. Liquid water and water vapor exist in dynamic phase equilibrium, so $\Delta G = 0$.
2. Vaporization requires heat input to break hydrogen bonds, so $\Delta H > 0$ (endothermic).
3. Gaseous steam has far greater spatial disorder than liquid water, so $\Delta S > 0$.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] If the equilibrium constant $K > 1$ for a reaction, then the value of $\Delta_r G^\circ$ must be:
questions.solution:
From $\Delta_r G^\circ = -2.303\, RT \log_{10} K$:
- If $K > 1$, then $\log_{10} K > 0$.
- Since $R > 0$ and $T > 0$, the product $-2.303 RT \log_{10} K$ must be negative.
- Therefore, $\Delta_r G^\circ < 0$ (the forward reaction is favored under standard state conditions).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Trouton's rule states that for a wide range of non-associated liquids, the molar entropy of vaporization at their normal boiling point is approximately equal to:
questions.solution:
**Trouton's Rule** observes that for most simple, non-polar and non-hydrogen-bonded liquids:
$$\Delta_{\text{vap}}S = \frac{\Delta_{\text{vap}}H}{T_b} \approx 85 - 88\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$
(Liquids with strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding like $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and ethanol show positive deviations from this value due to higher liquid-state order).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In which of the following processes is $\Delta S$ POSITIVE?
options: Condensation of water vapor into rain
questions.solution:
1. In $\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{H}(g)$, one diatomic molecule splits into two independent gaseous atoms, increasing the number of translating particles and microstates $\implies \Delta S > 0$.
2. Condensation and freezing convert fluids to more orderly states $\implies \Delta S < 0$.
3. In $2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{SO}_3(g)$, $3\text{ moles of gas}$ produce $2\text{ moles of gas}$ ($\Delta n_g = -1$) $\implies \Delta S < 0$.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] For a reaction with $\Delta_r H^\circ = +30.56\text{ kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta_r S^\circ = +66.0\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, at what minimum temperature does the reaction become spontaneous in the forward direction?
questions.solution:
For forward spontaneity, $\Delta G < 0$:
$$T > \frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{\Delta_r S^\circ} = \frac{30560\text{ J/mol}}{66.0\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}} \approx 463.03\text{ K} \approx 463\text{ K}$$

questions.question:
[NEET 2023] The standard molar entropies of $\text{N}_2(g), \text{H}_2(g),$ and $\text{NH}_3(g)$ are $191.5, 130.6,$ and $192.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. What is $\Delta_r S^\circ$ for the Haber synthesis:
$$\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(g)$$?
questions.solution:
Using standard molar entropies:
$$\Delta_r S^\circ = 2 S^\circ(\text{NH}_3) - [S^\circ(\text{N}_2) + 3 S^\circ(\text{H}_2)]$$
$$\Delta_r S^\circ = 2(192.3) - [191.5 + 3(130.6)]$$
$$\Delta_r S^\circ = 384.6 - [191.5 + 391.8] = 384.6 - 583.3 = -198.7\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] An ideal gas is expanded adiabatically against an opposing pressure of zero (free expansion). What are the values of $\Delta T, \Delta S_{\text{sys}},$ and $\Delta S_{\text{surr}}$?
questions.solution:
In an adiabatic free expansion into vacuum ($P_{\text{ext}} = 0, q = 0$):
1. $w = 0$, so $\Delta U = 0 \implies \Delta T = 0$.
2. Because the process is adiabatic and no heat is exchanged with the surroundings: $q_{\text{surr}} = 0 \implies \Delta S_{\text{surr}} = 0$.
3. The gas expands to fill a larger volume ($V_2 > V_1$), which is an irreversible spontaneous dispersion of matter: $\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = nR \ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$.
Thus, $\Delta T = 0, \Delta S_{\text{sys}} > 0,$ and $\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = 0$.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The Gibbs-Helmholtz equation relating enthalpy change and Gibbs energy change is given by:
questions.solution:
1. From fundamental thermodynamic relations, $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_p = -S$, which gives $\left[\frac{\partial(\Delta G)}{\partial T}\right]_p = -\Delta S$.
2. Substituting $-\Delta S = \left[\frac{\partial(\Delta G)}{\partial T}\right]_p$ into the definition $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$:
$$\Delta G = \Delta H + T\left[\frac{\partial(\Delta G)}{\partial T}\right]_p$$
This is the differential form of the **Gibbs-Helmholtz equation**.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] For the reaction $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$, $\Delta H = -20\text{ kJ/mol}$ and the activation energy is $E_a = 15\text{ kJ/mol}$. What is the activation energy for the reverse reaction $\text{B} \rightarrow \text{A}$?
questions.solution:
The relation between enthalpy of reaction and forward/reverse activation energies is:
$$\Delta H = E_{a(\text{forward})} - E_{a(\text{reverse})}$$
$$-20 = 15 - E_{a(\text{reverse})}$$
$$E_{a(\text{reverse})} = 15 - (-20) = 15 + 20 = 35\text{ kJ/mol}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following statements about entropy is INCORRECT?
options: At absolute zero temperature ($0\text{ K}$), the entropy of all substances is zero
Entropy is an extensive thermodynamic property
For a spontaneous process in an isolated system, $\Delta S > 0$
questions.solution:
1. The Third Law states that entropy approaches zero at $0\text{ K}$ strictly for **pure, perfectly crystalline substances**.
2. Substances with structural or orientation disorder (like $\text{CO}, \text{NO}, \text{N}_2\text{O}$, glass, and amorphous solid solutions) possess **residual entropy** ($S_0 > 0$) at $0\text{ K}$.
Therefore, Statement A is incorrect.

questions.question:
[NEET 2020] When graphite is converted into diamond under high pressure:
$$\text{C}(\text{graphite}) \rightarrow \text{C}(\text{diamond})$$
The entropy change ($\Delta S$) is negative because:
options: Diamond has a rigid, highly organized 3D tetrahedral framework with less positional disorder than layered graphite
Diamond has lower density than graphite
questions.solution:
1. Graphite has a layered planar sheet structure with relatively loose inter-layer van der Waals forces, allowing more vibrational/sliding degrees of freedom ($S^\circ \approx 5.74\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$).
2. Diamond has an extremely rigid, tightly packed, three-dimensional covalent tetrahedral network ($sp^3$) that restricts atomic motion ($S^\circ \approx 2.38\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$).
3. Thus, $\Delta S = S^\circ(\text{diamond}) - S^\circ(\text{graphite}) = 2.38 - 5.74 = -3.36\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1} < 0$.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] For a reaction with $\Delta_r G^\circ = 0$, the value of the equilibrium constant $K$ is:
questions.solution:
Using $\Delta_r G^\circ = -RT \ln K$:
$$\Delta_r G^\circ = 0 \implies -RT \ln K = 0 \implies \ln K = 0 \implies K = e^0 = 1$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A non-spontaneous reaction at all temperatures must have which combination of enthalpy and entropy changes?
questions.solution:
From $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$:
When $\Delta H > 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$:
$$\Delta G = (\text{positive}) - T(\text{negative}) = (\text{positive}) + T(\text{positive}) > 0$$
Because $\Delta G$ is positive at all temperatures, the reaction is never spontaneous.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Calculate the change in entropy when $1\text{ mole}$ of an ideal gas is heated from $300\text{ K}$ to $600\text{ K}$ at constant volume: (Given: $C_v = 1.5\, R$, $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 2 = 0.693$)
questions.solution:
At constant volume ($dV = 0$):
$$\Delta S = n C_v \ln\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)$$
Substitute $n = 1\text{ mol}$, $C_v = 1.5 R$, $T_1 = 300\text{ K}$, and $T_2 = 600\text{ K}$:
$$\Delta S = 1 \times (1.5 \times 8.314) \times \ln\left(\frac{600}{300}\right)$$
$$\Delta S = 12.471 \times \ln(2) = 12.471 \times 0.693 \approx 8.642\text{ J/K} \approx 8.64\text{ J/K}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When two non-reactive ideal gases are mixed together at constant temperature and pressure in an isolated chamber, the mixing process is spontaneous because:
questions.solution:
1. For ideal gases, intermolecular interactions are identical to those in pure gases, so no heat is evolved or absorbed upon mixing: $\Delta H_{\text{mix}} = 0$.
2. The mixing of two different gases increases spatial randomness and positional microstates, so $\Delta S_{\text{mix}} = -n R \sum X_i \ln X_i > 0$.
3. Therefore, $\Delta G_{\text{mix}} = \Delta H_{\text{mix}} - T\Delta S_{\text{mix}} = -T\Delta S_{\text{mix}} < 0$.
The process is driven entirely by the positive entropy of mixing.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] For the reaction $2\text{A}(g) + \text{B}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{D}(g)$, $\Delta U^\circ = -10.5\text{ kJ}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = -44.1\text{ J/K}$ at $298\text{ K}$. The standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^\circ$) for the reaction is: (Take $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
1. Calculate $\Delta n_g$:
$$\Delta n_g = 2 - (2 + 1) = 2 - 3 = -1$$
2. Calculate $\Delta H^\circ$:
$$\Delta H^\circ = \Delta U^\circ + \Delta n_g RT = -10500 + (-1 \times 8.314 \times 298) = -10500 - 2477.6 = -12977.6\text{ J} = -12.98\text{ kJ}$$
3. Calculate $\Delta G^\circ$:
$$\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ = -12977.6 - [298 \times (-44.1)] = -12977.6 - (-13141.8) = -12977.6 + 13141.8 = +164.2\text{ J} \approx +0.16\text{ kJ}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] The unit of entropy in the SI system is:
questions.solution:
Entropy is defined by the relation $\Delta S = \frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$.
- Unit of heat ($q$): Joules ($\text{J}$)
- Unit of absolute temperature ($T$): Kelvin ($\text{K}$)
Thus, molar entropy is expressed in **$\text{J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$** (or $\text{J/K}$ for total entropy).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An endothermic reaction is spontaneous at room temperature ($298\text{ K}$). It must be true that:
questions.solution:
1. For an endothermic reaction: $\Delta H > 0$.
2. For the reaction to be spontaneous: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$.
3. This requires $\Delta S > 0$ and the entropy term $T\Delta S$ must be larger in magnitude than the endothermic enthalpy term $\Delta H$ ($T\Delta S > \Delta H$), overcoming the unfavorable enthalpy change.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When rust forms on iron via the reaction $4\text{Fe}(s) + 3\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3(s)$, the entropy of the system decreases ($\Delta S_{\text{sys}} < 0$). Why is rusting spontaneous?
options: The reaction is highly exothermic, releasing heat to the surroundings such that $\Delta S_{\text{surr}} > 0$ and $\Delta S_{\text{total}} > 0$
Iron atoms gain volume upon rusting
Rusting violates the Second Law of Thermodynamics
questions.solution:
1. In rusting, $3\text{ moles of gas}$ are consumed to form a solid oxide, so the system's entropy decreases ($\Delta S_{\text{sys}} < 0$).
2. However, the oxidation of iron is strongly **exothermic** ($\Delta H_{\text{sys}} \ll 0$).
3. The heat released into the surroundings increases the entropy of the surroundings:
$$\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = -\frac{\Delta H_{\text{sys}}}{T} > 0$$
4. Because $\Delta S_{\text{surr}}$ is much larger in magnitude than $|\Delta S_{\text{sys}}|$, the total entropy of the universe increases:
$$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{sys}} + \Delta S_{\text{surr}} > 0$$
Hence, the process obeys the Second Law and is spontaneous.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] For a reversible reaction, if $\Delta_r G^\circ < 0$, which of the following statements is correct regarding the equilibrium state?
questions.solution:
From $\Delta_r G^\circ = -RT \ln K$:
$$\ln K = -\frac{\Delta_r G^\circ}{RT}$$
If $\Delta_r G^\circ < 0$ (negative), then $\ln K > 0$, which implies $K > 1$.
An equilibrium constant greater than $1$ signifies that products predominate over reactants at equilibrium.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] The entropy of vaporization of a liquid is $85\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and its enthalpy of vaporization is $34.0\text{ kJ/mol}$. The boiling point of the liquid is:
questions.solution:
At the normal boiling point:
$$T_b = \frac{\Delta_{\text{vap}}H}{\Delta_{\text{vap}}S}$$
$$\Delta_{\text{vap}}H = 34.0\text{ kJ/mol} = 34000\text{ J/mol}$$
$$\Delta_{\text{vap}}S = 85\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$$
$$T_b = \frac{34000}{85} = 400\text{ K}$$
$$T_b = 400 - 273 = 127^\circ\text{C}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A system undergoes a spontaneous change under isothermal and isobaric conditions. The maximum useful non-expansion electrical work ($w_{\text{non-PV}}$) that can be obtained from the system is equal to:
questions.solution:
1. Under conditions of constant temperature and pressure, the decrease in Gibbs free energy ($-\Delta G$) represents the **maximum useful work** (other than pressure-volume work of expansion) that can be extracted from a system:
$$w_{\text{net, max}} = -\Delta G$$
2. In electrochemical cells, this corresponds directly to the electrical work produced: $-\Delta G = nFE_{\text{cell}}$.
